La Casa Vella

A retreat among vineyards, pine woods and Montserrat

BreatheShall we start?

Rural stay since 1898

The house

La Casa Vella is our family's village house in El Bedorc, a small retreat surrounded by vineyards. Original stone walls and quiet in every corner.

Barcelona, the Penedès wineries and the castles of the area are close by. But here, mornings start slowly.

Restored with care

Walls that hold more than a century of stories

Stone that has seen generations come and go, exposed wooden ceilings and corners restored with patience and affection. The house keeps the soul of traditional architecture, and now also all the comfort to stay a few days without watching the clock.

Restaurant

From morning coffee to a glass of wine

Our restaurant is on the ground floor: a space of warm light, stone and wood to start the day with a good coffee and end it with a glass of Penedès wine.

In season, the terrace fills with the smell of calçots on the grill. It's the corner where there's always someone from the family, ready to suggest routes and places nearby.

The story of Casa Parellada

A farmhouse brought back to life

  1. 1898

    Building the house

    The house was built between 1898 and 1900.

  2. 20th century

    Years of farming

    For many years the owners lived off the land.

  3.  

    The extension

    A pigsty, a henhouse and a small stable were added for “Macho”, the horse that worked the land and carried the harvest.

  4.  

    The empty house

    The family grew old and, with no one to follow, the house was left empty.

  5. Today

    La Casa Vella

    Now it is part of our family's project.

The house in pictures

The area

El Bedorc, with Montserrat in view

El Bedorc is a small paradise in the heart of the Anoia: vineyards, woods and farmland close to the Penedès wineries. From the house, Montserrat's silhouette marks the horizon.

On foot or by bike, routes start at the front door: paths through vineyards, hermitages and villages with history.

  • Sant Sadurní d'Anoia15 min
  • Montserrat45 min
  • Barcelona45 min
  • Barcelona Airport50 min
Near the house

Places to explore

In El Bedorc itself

La Ventosa castle

The stones of the castle the village grew around, recorded over a thousand years ago. A short walk to start the day.

15 min

Sant Sadurní d'Anoia

The capital of cava. Century-old cellars, tastings among the vines and bubbles for a toast at sunset.

20 min

Capellades

The Paper Mill Museum and the Bassa pool, where water has turned mills for centuries.

25 min

Vilafranca del Penedès

The heart of the Penedès: the Vinseum, the market and, at the town festival, the castellers in the square.

30 min

Claramunt castle

A medieval fortress on the hilltop, with the whole Anoia at its feet.

45 min

Montserrat

The mountain you see from the house: the monastery, the boys' choir and paths up to Sant Jeroni.

Guides

Plan your visit

Guides

Calçot season 2026-2027: dates and the Valls festival

Calçot season runs from November to April. The 2027 Gran Festa de la Calçotada in Valls is on Sunday 31 January and marks the start of the high season.

15 min from the house

Cava cellars in Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, 15 minutes from El Bedorc

Sant Sadurní d'Anoia, the capital of cava, is 15 minutes from La Casa Vella. Codorníu, Freixenet and other cellars can be visited if you book ahead, and the cava fair is in October.

45 min from the house

Montserrat from El Bedorc: how to get up and what to do in a day

Montserrat is about 45 minutes by car from La Casa Vella. You can drive up to the monastery, take the rack railway from Monistrol or the cable car, and the classic path climbs to Sant Jeroni, at 1,236 metres.
